# Copilot Instructions for TaskFlow

TaskFlow is a web-based project management app for students, study groups and small teams. Users create projects, add members, assign tasks and track progress on a dashboard.

## Tech stack

- Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript in strict mode
- Tailwind CSS v4 (no `tailwind.config`; design tokens go in `globals.css` with `@theme`)
- Geist font, loaded with `next/font`
- PostgreSQL on Neon, accessed with Prisma 7.10.1
- Hosting: Vercel
- ESLint and Prettier

Authentication (Auth.js v5 or Clerk) and automated testing are not decided yet. Do not assume either exists. Do not add an auth library, a test framework or a UI library (such as shadcn/ui) unless the team approves it.

## Project structure

- `app/`: routes, using the App Router
- `components/`: reusable components
- `prisma/schema.prisma`: data model
- `prisma/migrations/`: migrations
- `generated/prisma/`: generated Prisma Client (git-ignored, created by `prisma generate`)

## Data model

Entities: `User`, `Project`, `ProjectMember` (join table with a `role`) and `Task`. The source of truth is `prisma/schema.prisma`.

- Task status enum: `TODO`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`. Use these exact uppercase values everywhere. Never create lowercase variants.
- Project role enum: `OWNER`, `MEMBER`.
- Reuse the types generated by Prisma. Do not write duplicate hand-made types for these models.
- Do not edit existing migrations. Schema changes need a new migration through a pull request.

## Coding conventions

- Use TypeScript strictly. Do not use `any`.
- Use Server Components by default. Add `"use client"` only when the component needs browser interactivity (state, effects, event handlers, `usePathname`).
- Validate untrusted input (forms and API requests) on the server.
- Every project and task operation must check authorization on the server. Never rely on hiding UI.
- Never store plaintext passwords. Never commit secrets or connection strings.
- Components use PascalCase file names (`ProjectCard.tsx`). Functions and variables use camelCase.
- Prefer small, reusable components. Reuse `Button`, `FormField`, `Badge`, `NavLink`, `PageHeader` and `EmptyState` instead of recreating them.

## Styling and design

- Use Tailwind utility classes. Write custom CSS only when necessary.
- Palette: `indigo-600` for primary actions, `slate` for neutrals, `red-700` for errors, `emerald-700` for success.
- Task status badges: To Do `bg-slate-100 text-slate-800`, In Progress `bg-amber-100 text-amber-900`, Completed `bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-900`. Always show the status as text, never by color alone.
- Spacing uses multiples of 4 px (`2, 4, 6, 8, 12`). Avoid arbitrary values.
- Page container: `mx-auto max-w-6xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`.
- Cards: `rounded-xl border border-slate-200 bg-white p-6 shadow-sm`. Buttons and inputs: `rounded-lg`, minimum height `h-10`.
- Write mobile-first and enlarge with `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`. No dark mode in the MVP.

## Accessibility

- Use semantic HTML and keyboard-operable controls.
- Every input has a visible label. Form errors use `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.
- The active navigation link uses `aria-current="page"`.
- Every interactive element has a visible focus style: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-indigo-600 focus-visible:ring-offset-2`.

## Planned routes

`/`, `/register`, `/login`, `/dashboard`, `/projects/new`, `/projects/[projectId]`, `/profile`.

## Open decisions

- Authentication provider and session strategy
- Project sharing/invitation flow details
- Automated test framework and CI/testing strategy
- Deployment/testing environments

Document and follow team decisions once made; do not silently introduce conflicting approaches.

## Git workflow

- Create a feature branch from an updated `main` (`feature/...`, `fix/...`, `docs/...`).
- Use clear commit messages such as `feat: ...`, `fix: ...`, `docs: ...`.
- Open a pull request into `main`. At least one teammate should review it.
- Never run `prisma migrate dev`, `migrate reset` or `db push` against the shared database.
- Install dependencies with `npm ci`. Do not run `npm install prisma@latest`: Prisma and `@prisma/client` are pinned to 7.10.1.

## Notes for AI assistance

- Treat this file as team guidance, but verify against the current code and docs before making changes.
- Prefer incremental, verifiable progress that matches acceptance criteria.
- If a requested change depends on an open decision (auth/db/tests), state the assumption and implement the smallest compatible foundation.
